listing_status: private — "wholly owned subsidiary of Arkansas Electric Cooperatives, Inc. (AECI)" (every ERMCO release; TNECD 2019). No exchange listing, no public financial statements found.
name: ERMCO, Inc. (Electric Research and Manufacturing Cooperative, Inc.)

capacity_indicators: 8 millionth unit (Aug-2023 AECI magazine) → 9 millionth (2025-06-20 ceremony); 1st million took 258 months, 8th took 27 months — source: https://arkansaslivingmagazine.com/story/ermco-inc-celebrates-8-million-milestone/
Employees: 30 (1972) → 1,450+ Dyersburg (2021) → ~2,000 (Nov-2024) → ~3,500 incl. affiliates (2025–26) → 3,700+ (2026 history page)
profile.end_markets: North American utilities — co-ops, public power, investor-owned utilities (e.g., Exelon received the 9 millionth unit; Arizona Public Service pad-mount supplier since 2021, APS Supplier Excellence Award 2025), renewable energy, commercial & industrial, data centers (via Pioneer/V&F). "shipping thousands of transformers across the US and Canada".
profile.owners: Arkansas Electric Cooperatives, Inc. (AECI), a cooperative owned by Arkansas distribution co-ops — ERMCO is a wholly owned subsidiary.

profile.products: Liquid-filled (oil) distribution transformers: single-phase pole-mount 1/2–250 kVA (2.4–34.5 kV, 150 kV BIL); three-phase pole/platform-mount; single-phase pad-mount 5–250 kVA (Type 1/2, TrimLine, MicroTrim); three-phase pad-mount 30–3,000 kVA (2.4–35 kV, 150 kV BIL); Eco-Pad junction cabinets (ERMCO Distribution Transformers, Dyersburg TN). Via Spire (2022): Power Partners — single/three-phase pole-mount and single-phase pad-mount (Athens GA, >9M units produced); Pioneer Transformers — three-phase pad-mount and substation transformers up to 10 MVA / 69 kV (350 kV BIL), submersible, network, grounding (Granby QC); ERMCO Dry Type / V&F — custom dry-type transformers & magnetics for OEMs, data centers, EV, renewables (Celina TN). ERMCO Components (ECI) — expulsion fuses, arrester disconnects, HV/LV bushings, circuit breakers, dry-well fuseholders (Greeneville TN; Reynosa MX; Antioch IL/Bristol WI per site). Scale: >650,000 transformers made in 2024; >9,500 shipped weekly; 3,700+ employees (2026).

structural_breaks.note: GridBridge (Raleigh, NC; power-electronics grid solutions) acquired (year only in source).
~$12M expansion into a third Dyersburg building (ex-Caterpillar), 150 jobs; CEO: business up >10%/yr for five years.

Spire Power Solutions L.P. (Athens, GA) bought from Mill Point Capital — brands Power Partners (Athens GA pole/pad), Pioneer Transformers (Granby QC), Jefferson Electric (dry-type), V&F Transformer (dry-type OEM); Spire had >1,000 staff and 5 facilities in GA, TN, TX, Canada, Mexico. Month from Lincoln International 2022 deal note + AECI magazine Feb-2023 ("recently acquired"); day not stated.
Jefferson Electric (dry-type LV/MV transformers) sold to Mill Point Capital to form Voltaris Power; ERMCO keeps liquid-filled + V&F dry-type.
Three-phase Dyersburg capacity expansion in three phases, 400 jobs, backed by $54.1M tax-credit (NMTC) financing; ERMCO ~2,000 staff, >9,500 transformers/week (TECA report).

9 millionth transformer; >$70M planned in next 12 months to expand Dyersburg three-phase capacity and add amorphous-steel core lines (DOE 2029 standard); new 160,000 sq ft Bristol, WI facility launched; Granby, QC expansion.
New 566,121 sq ft three-phase plant in Waddell, Maricopa County, AZ (first west of the Mississippi), >500 jobs, operational 2027.
